reflections.title: "Get Up into the High Mountain"

reflect.text: Growing in our walk with Christ is like climbing a tall mountain. When we first begin at the base, our sight is limited, and we catch only a small glimpse of who he is. But as we walk with him through years of trials, each experience lifts us higher. With every step upward, our view widens, and we discover far more of the boundless love and faithfulness of our Savior.

Too often, though, we settle for the spiritual lowlands. We live in dim valleys like workers trapped in dark mines who never see the warm sunlight. We get comfortable with small spiritual attainments when God invites us to breathe the fresh air of his presence. Charles Spurgeon urges us to leave coldness behind and "aspire to a higher, a nobler, a fuller life." The Lord calls us to lift our hearts and draw nearer to him.

questions: Where have you settled for spiritual sluggishness instead of seeking to know Christ more deeply?
What is one practical way you can climb higher and draw closer to the Lord today?
reflections.prayer: Lord Jesus, do not let us remain content in the spiritual valleys or live in the dark. Give us a deep thirst to climb higher and see more of your glory. Draw us close to yourself so that we may walk in the full liberty of your presence. Amen.

reflections.title: "He Gathers the Lambs"

reflect.text: Like fragile sheep, we easily panic, lose our way, and wander into trouble through our stubborn self-will. We are completely unable to rescue ourselves. Yet Jesus is the Good Shepherd who gave his life for his broken flock. He never drives us with harshness. Instead, he walks ahead of us, calls us gently, and deeply understands our struggles because he took on our human nature.

In God's flock, some believers are strong, while others are timid, weak, or young in faith. Our Shepherd does not hand over our care to anyone else; he rescues and keeps us personally. When the lambs lag behind or grow weary, he scoops them up in his mighty arms and holds them against his chest. As Charles Spurgeon reminds us, safely in his bosom, "they must hurt the Shepherd first" before any enemy can harm them.

questions: Which of your current weaknesses or fears do you need to place into the Shepherd's arms?
How does knowing that Jesus holds you close to his heart help you trust his guidance?
reflections.prayer: Good Shepherd, thank you for seeking us out when we wander and holding us in your strong, loving arms. Help us remember that our daily struggles are never trivial to you. Grant us simple faith to rest near your heart and listen to your gentle voice. Amen.

D5.work: In the Bosom of the Shepherd

unsupported.text: Because Christ holds his people so close, we can be sure that none of our daily troubles are too small for his notice. He sees every sigh, every tear, and every weakness. He protects us from danger and patiently restores us whenever we stumble.

reflections.title: Renewing Strength in the Lord

reflect.text: Hectic schedules, loneliness, and pressure often leave us exhausted. In difficult seasons, God's people sometimes make the mistake of thinking the Lord has forgotten them or grown tired. We repeat that error whenever we rely solely on our own willpower or turn to empty escapes for relief. Just like an electrical appliance is useless when unplugged from the wall, our lives run out of power when we try to live apart from God.

The prophet Isaiah reminds us that the everlasting Creator never grows weary, and his understanding has no limit. The strength he offers is not self-help or positive thinking, but supernatural power supplied by his Holy Spirit. When we turn away from counterfeit comforts and patiently wait upon him, our inner souls are renewed. Keeping our eyes on his greatness gives us the power to run without tiring and walk without fainting.

questions: What counterfeit comforts do you turn to when you feel drained by life?
How can you practice waiting on the Lord this week instead of relying on your own strength?
reflections.prayer: Everlasting God, forgive us for trying to live by our own power and running to empty escapes when we are tired. Thank you that you never grow weary and your understanding is beyond measure. Fill us with your Holy Spirit and renew our strength so we can faithfully walk with you today. Amen.
